# libds architecture

How libds, the reference runtime, is built: its module
decomposition, public surfaces, dependency discipline,
compiler / runtime split, and build artefacts.

This doc is the **"how"** of libds. The **"what"** —
what every conforming runtime must provide — lives at [RARC].
Treat the runtime-spec subsystem names (consumption
loop, working memory, Rete, agenda, dispatcher,
recorder) as fixed vocabulary; this doc picks
where each one lives in libds code.

## What this is not

- Not the abstract runtime spec.
  [RARC] is authoritative for that; this doc implements it.
- Not an API reference. The public surface is
  `runtime/include/libds.h`.
- Not a data-model spec. Struct layouts and ownership
  rules are [IDAT]; allocation
  routing is [IALC]; the error
  model is [IERR].
- Not a threading design. libds spawns no threads and
  does not sleep or block ([IARC.1.10]); the runtime spec
  commits to single-writer consumption per tier, and the
  integrator owns whatever thread calls in.
